<meta>This page contains a Sanskrit manuscript transcription from the eleventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, the Vision of the Universal Form (Vishvarupa Darshana Yoga). The OCR contains several reading errors and phonetic variations typical of handwritten palm-leaf manuscripts, which have been reconciled with the standard text of verses 22 through 25.</meta>

# 45 Recto

The hosts of <term>Siddhas</term> <gloss>perfected beings</gloss> cry out "May there be peace!" and praise you with magnificent hymns. The <term>Rudras</term> <gloss>gods of storms</gloss>, the <term>Adityas</term> <gloss>solar deities</gloss>, the <term>Vasus</term> <gloss>elemental gods</gloss>, the <term>Sadhyas</term> <gloss>celestial guardians</gloss>, the <term>Vishvedevas</term> <gloss>universal gods</gloss>, the two <term>Ashvins</term> <gloss>divine physicians</gloss>, the <term>Maruts</term> <gloss>wind deities</gloss>, and the ancestors <note>verse 22</note>. 

The hosts of <term>Gandharvas</term> <gloss>celestial musicians</gloss>, <term>Yakshas</term> <gloss>nature spirits</gloss>, <term>Asuras</term> <gloss>demons</gloss>, and <term>Siddhas</term> all gaze upon you in total amazement <note>verse 22 continued</note>. Seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed one, with many arms, thighs, and feet, with many bellies and many formidable tusks, the worlds are terrified, and so am I <note>verse 23</note>.

Touching the sky, glowing with many colors, with mouths wide open and large shining eyes, seeing you thus, my inner soul is trembling with fear. I find no steadiness or peace, O Vishnu <note>verse 24</note>. Seeing your mouths formidable with tusks, resembling the fire of time <gloss>the fire of cosmic destruction</gloss>—

---

# 45 Verso

—I do not know the directions, nor do I find any comfort. Be gracious, O Lord of Gods, O Refuge of the Universe <note>verse 25</note>. 

<meta>The remaining lines on the verso appear to be repetitive liturgical refrains or scribal colophons mentioning Sudhama, a devotee or patron, and various auspicious phrases for fame and glory which deviate from the standard Gita text.</meta>

Here, may Sudhama always have fame, without enemies, among the hosts of gods. Joy in battle, may Sudhama always have fame, without enemies. The learned <term>Bhatta</term> <gloss>scholar</gloss> has attained the goal in every direction. Fame without enemies. 

Now, with the sacrifice... <note>verse 21 reference</note>. As Joy... <note>verse 22 reference</note>. Here, may Sudhama always have fame, without enemies. The various great ones... <note>verse 23 reference</note>. Here, may Sudhama always have fame, without enemies.

<note>A circular hole is carved into the center of the palm leaf to accommodate the binding cord that holds the manuscript together.</note>

<summary>This page describes Arjuna's overwhelming vision of Krishna's universal form, listing the celestial beings who witness it and expressing Arjuna's deep terror. The verso includes non-canonical scribal additions or prayers for a patron named Sudhama.</summary>

<keywords>Bhagavad Gita, Vishvarupa, Krishna, Arjuna, Deities, Sanskrit Manuscript, Sudhama, Universal Form</keywords>
